parramatta|secondary_street_setback|dwel.note: Correct, and ALREADY IN PRODUCTION: dcp_setback_controls holds parramatta / dwelling_house / 3m / section_ref '3.3.1.2 C.06' / pdf_page 60, from the same clause. parramatta|secondary_street_setback|dual.note: NEW. Part 3.3 heading is 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT DWELLING HOUSES, SECONDARY DWELLINGS AND DUAL OCCUPANCIES'; 3.3.2 is the dual occupancy sub-part. 'On corner lots, the secondary street setback must also be a minimum of 3 metres' - a minimum, so value_min is the requirement; no concession to strand in the condition; ground level; general to the LGA, not a precinct.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|seco.note: NEW. 3.3.3 is the secondary dwellings sub-part of Part 3.3. Clause reads 'On corner lots, the secondary street setback must setback a minimum of 3 metres' - the doubled verb is the document's own wording, not an extraction artifact. applicability secondary_dwelling_specific is right: it is the granny-flat control, not the house control.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|mult.note: Correct, and ALREADY IN PRODUCTION: parramatta / multi_dwelling_housing / 4m / '3.4.1.2 C.08' / pdf_page 80. Same clause, same value, independently reproduced. Not re-inserted.

TERRACE HOUSING (page carries 'Figure 3.4.2.2.1 - Terrace Housing Site Setbacks'). The DCP files terraces under the MULTI-DWELLING HOUSING heading and states the same 4m, so as a served row this is identical to the existing 3.4.1.2 C.08 multi_dwelling_housing 4m row: same dev_type, same value. It corroborates rather than adds, so it stops here. Serving both would hand a consumer two rows that answer one question.

NEW, and the dev_type was WRONG in a way that would have served a contradiction. The page states 'manor houses shall be a maximum of 2-storeys', so this clause's subject is manor houses - but it sits under the MULTI-DWELLING HOUSING heading and was proposed as dev_type multi_dwelling_housing at 3m. Parramatta already serves multi_dwelling_housing at 4m. Two rows, one dev_type, 4m and 3m, with nothing in dev_type to tell them apart. Corrected to dev_type manor_house, which is the clause's own subject and an existing value in the table's vocabulary. No number changed.

corrections.condition: Manor houses (Part 3.4.3, filed by the DCP under Multi-Dwelling Housing). On corner lots, to the secondary street frontage.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|resi.note: NEW. Page heading 'RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT APARTMENT BUILDINGS', part 3.5.1. 'Buildings must be set back a minimum of 3 metres from the secondary street or laneway frontage'. GRAIN checked: this is the building setback, not an upper-level massing control, and the clause's stated purpose (threshold to ground floor apartments, boundary landscaping) confirms ground level. 'or laneway' is in the condition, correctly - it widens what counts as the secondary frontage, it does not change the number.

SCOPE and GRAIN, and the quote says so itself. The source is 'Podium Primary and secondary 3m road boundary' - an interleaved table cell from the Oxford Street, Epping precinct, governing the primary AND secondary boundary together at podium level. Three faults at once: precinct-scoped, combined-frontage, and not ground level. Parramatta's real general answer for apartments is the 3m in 3.5.1.2 C.04 above; serving this beside it adds a precinct figure that a consumer cannot distinguish from the general one.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|mult.note: SCOPE. Page heading is '8.3.1 HARRIS PARK' - a named precinct. The clause also reads 'Setback from rear lanes and/or secondary streets', conflating a rear-lane setback with a secondary-street setback into one figure, so even within Harris Park it does not answer the question this control_type asks. Two proposals were made from this one clause (multi_dwelling_housing and residential_flat_building); both are rejected on the same ground.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|univ.note: The clause says 'front setback along Weston and Hope Streets', not secondary setback. Reading it as secondary depends on inferring from a neighbouring clause (C.03, 7m to Arthur Street) which frontage is primary - that is reasoning about the document, not reading it, and this control type must be stated not deduced. Compounded by scope: 'Key Block Three, Harris Park Special Areas' is a named block.

parramatta|secondary_street_setback|mixe.note: SCOPE at its narrowest: a control for one address, 33-34 Marion Street, Harris Park, and a podium-level setback at that. 'Minimum 4 metre setback to the south (Peace Lane)' is a correct reading of a site-specific figure. Served as parramatta's secondary street setback it would be wrong for every other site in the LGA.
